Order: (Per Smt.Dr.G.Radha Rani, Hon'ble President)
1. This appeal is filed by Opposite Party No.1 aggrieved by the order
dated 30.07.2021 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal
Commission, Nalgonda in CC.No.70/2020 directing the Opposite Parties 1
and 2 jointly and severally to pay an amount of Rs.18,597/- to the
Complainant towards costs of the return flight ticket with interest @ 9%
p.a. from the date of booking of flight ticket i.e., 07.12.2018 till realization,
Rs.10,000/- towards compensation for mental agony and Rs.3,000/-
towards costs.
2. The parties are hereinafter referred as arrayed before the District
Commission as Complainant and Opposite Parties 1 and 2.
3. The case of the Complainant was that, the Opposite Party No.1 was
a travel agency having Head Office in Gurugram providing a range of
choice of hotels, flights, trains, buses and cars for travellers. Opposite
Party No.2 was an Interim Resolution Professional for Jet Airways. The
Complainant approached Opposite Party No.1 online for booking flight
ticket on Ukraine International Airlines and Jet Airways on 07.12.2018 for
his friend Ms.Lilla Petofalvi, a Hungarian citizen for the journey date
11.12.2018 from Budapest-Kiev-New Delhi and availed the service. The
return journey was from New Delhi-Mumbai-Paris-Budapest on
02.06.2019 on Jet Airways 9W-384, 9W-124, 9W-4966, PNR TVFRZZ. The
Complainant paid an amount of Rs.26,667/- for Ukraine International
Airlines PS-814 PNR U6FHU7 towards one way journey and for the return
journey paid an amount of Rs.18,597/- through his SBI Bank account.
The Complainant's friend i.e., Hungarian citizen received an email from
Opposite Party No.1 on 24.04.2019 about Jet Airways flight cancellation
notification booking code TVFRZZ and asked to apply for refund.
Immediately Complainant emailed to Opposite Party No.1 for refund of the
ticket amount of Rs.18,597/- and submitted all required documents
demanded by Opposite Party No.1 for refund process. The Complainant
3
also gave his bank account details where the refund money could be
transferred, but as the ticket amount was not refunded, the Complainant
got issued a legal notice to Opposite Parties 1 and 2 on 27.09.2019. On
01.11.2019, Opposite Party No.1 gave a reply notice to the Complainant
and requested for some more documents. The Complainant sent the
required documents to Opposite Party No.1 on 25.11.2020, but the
Opposite Parties did not refund the said amount and dragged the matter
on one pretext or other. As such the Complainant filed the Consumer
Complaint demanding an amount of Rs.18,597/- + Rs.8,071/- (interest @
24% p.a. from 07.12.2018 to 28.09.2020 on Rs.18,597/-) + Rs.2,00,000/-
towards mental agony and damages, a total amount of Rs.2,26,668/-.
4. Notice served on Opposite Party No.1 on 20.04.2021 and served on
Opposite Party No.2 on 19.03.2021 but they failed to appear before the
District Commission and contest the matter.
5. The Complainant filed his proof affidavit as PW1 and got marked
Ex.A1 to A8.
6. The District Commission on considering the material on record,
allowed the complaint in part directing Opposite Parties 1 and 2 jointly
and severally to pay the amount of Rs.18,597/-, the ticket amount with
interest @ 9% p.a. from 07.12.2018 till realization and awarded
Rs.10,000/- towards mental agony and Rs.3,000/- towards costs.
7. Aggrieved by the said order passed by the District Commission, the
Opposite Party No.1 preferred this appeal contending that:
 Opposite Party No.1 is the CEO of GOIBIBO Company which in turn
 was only a facilitator which provides an online platform for
 purchase of tickets. The Company had duly booked the tickets in
 the airline as mentioned by the Complainant for such dates as
 requested by the Complainant. Opposite Party No.1 could not be
4
held responsible for the fault of the airline as he was not responsible
 for the day-to-day affairs of the Company.
 The Company had never proceeded to cancel the ticket. On the
 contrary, it was the airline, Jet Airways on which the Complainant
 had chosen to book the tickets which had cancelled the operation of
 its flights.
 The amount paid by the Complainant i.e., Rs.18,597/-was towards
 flight ticket paid by Opposite Party No.1 on behalf of the
 Complainant to the airline. Jet Airways in which the Complainant
 sought to book the ticket issued the E-ticket on receiving the
 amount towards the ticket.
 If at all the Complainant was entitled for refund, the same was
 liable to be refunded by the airline in which the Complainant
 proceeded to book the tickets. The Complainant failed to implead
 the airline in which he booked the ticket as a party to the
 proceeding. The proceedings were not maintainable as against the
 Opposite Party No.1 or the Company.
 The order passed by the District Forum suffers from non-application
 of mind. It mechanically held Opposite Party No.1 as liable for
 deficiency in service.
 The District Forum failed to appreciate the fact that the services
 that were offered by Opposite Party No.1 were limited to booking an
 air ticket in the choice of the airline selected by the Complainant.
 The CEO of GOIBBIO could not be arrayed as Opposite Party as he
 was not responsible for the day-to-day affairs of the organization.
 Therefore, the complaint suffers from mis-joinder of necessary
 parties. The District Commission ought to have directed the
 Complainant to relieve Opposite Party No.1 and to implead
 necessary parties to the complaint.
 The District Forum failed to consider the Circular issued by the
 Office of the Director General of Civil Aviation, Government of India
 issued in furtherance to Rule-133A of the Aircraft Rules and
5
Ministry of Civil Aviation Order No.AV/13030/105/2007-DT dated
 12th May 2008 whereby the said authority categorically issued a
 mandate that in case of purchase of ticket through travel
 agent/portal, onus of refund shall lie with the airlines, as agents are
 their appointed representatives only and that the airlines shall
 ensure that the refund process is completed within 30 working
 days.
 The judgment relied by the District Forum in not applicable to the
 facts and circumstances of the present case. Shutting down
 operations of the airlines was mismanagement of airlines by its
 management and it was well within their control to stop the same
 from happening.
 Opposite Party No.1 Company themselves had duly informed the
 Complainant about the cancellation of the flight by the airline and
 duly advised the Complainant to apply for refund out of concern for
 the money of the Complainant.
 The District Commission held Opposite Party No.1 liable for the
 action of Opposite Party No.2 without application of mind under a
 misconceived understanding of the case.
 In the light of the Civil Aviation requirements issued by the Director
 General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), the District Forum ought to have
 dismissed the complaint.
 The Opposite Party No.1 further contended that the District Forum
 failed to take note of the fact that while insolvency proceedings were
 in progress against Opposite Party No.2, no creditors can be paid till
 a final resolution plan was approved and executed. Insolvency
 proceedings against Jet Airways was still ongoing and pending
 before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). As such, the
 District Forum ought to have deferred the case till the proceedings
 before NCLT reached some finality;
and prayed to set aside the impugned order passed by the District
Commission, Nalgonda.
6
8. Notice was served on Respondent No.1. Respondent No.1 present in
person on 15.03.2022 but thereafter failed to appear before the Forum.
The Appellant also failed to appear before the Forum. The Appellant failed
to take out the personal notice on Respondent No.2 as ordered by the
Forum, as such the appeal was dismissed against Respondent No.2. No
representation for the Appellant and Respondent No.1 for the past many
years. Considering that the appeal is of the year 2021, we proceeded to
decide the matter on merits.
9. The points for consideration are:
(i) Whether the exparte order passed against the
 Appellant/Opposite Party No.1 by the District Commission
 warrants any interference?
(ii) Whether the Appellant travel agency is liable for deficiency in
 service?
(iii) Whether the CEO was rightly fastened with liability?
(iv) To what relief?

10. Point No.(i):
It is not in dispute that the Appellant remained exparte before the
District Commission. The explanation offered by him was that due to
Covid-19 Pandemic and employees working from home, the Appellant
could not attend the proceedings. However, no material particulars such
as the relevant dates of hearings, nature of restrictions in courts during
the said period with any documentary proof had been placed on record by
the Appellant/Opposite Party No.1. It is pertinent to note that during the
Pandemic period, Consumer Fora were functioning through virtual mode
and the Complainant filed his proof affidavit and also documents during
the said period. But the Appellant had not explained as to why no written
version was filed or why no representation was made through counsel.
Mere bald assertions without supporting evidence does not constitute
7
sufficient cause. Hence, no ground is made out to set aside the exparte
order passed against them.
11. Point No.(ii):
The contention of the Appellant was that the airline alone was
responsible and that its services were limited to that of booking an air
ticket in the choice of the airline selected by the Complainant. The
Complainant booked the ticket through the Appellant establishing the
consumer/service provider relationship within the meaning of the
Consumer Protection Act, 2019
. Even if Jet Airways cancels the flight, the
Appellant cannot escape liability as it was the Appellant who facilitated
the booking and received consideration. The Appellant had a duty to assist
the consumer in securing refund. The consumer cannot be compelled to
chase multiple entities for redressal. Failure to refund or facilitate refund
amounts to deficiency in service. Merely shifting the blame to Jet Airways
is not a complete defense. Even if the airline cancelled the flight, the agent
had a continuing obligation to assist in refund processing and to ensure
that the customer is not left remediless. Failure to secure or facilitate
refund amounts to deficiency in service. Travel agents cannot wash their
hands off after ticket issuance, as they were accountable to the extent of
refund facilitation or refund liability, especially when money passed
through them. The District Commission rightly appreciated the said
aspect.
12. The Appellants relied upon the Circular of the DGCA vide File
No.23-16/2016-AED dated 22.05.2008 regarding refund of airline tickets
to passengers of public transport undertaking wherein it was stated in 3(c)
that,
 "in case of purchase of ticket through travel agent/portal, onus of
refund shall lie with the airlines as agents are their appointed
representatives. The airlines shall ensure that the refund process is
completed within 30 working days."
8
The DGCA primarily places the responsibility on the airline to
refund money. But however, the same would not absolve the travel agent
of its obligation towards the consumer particularly when the booking was
facilitated through it. The consumer cannot be relegated to pursue
remedies only against the airline. The reliance placed on the Circular
issued by the Director General of Civil Aviation by the Appellant/Opposite
Party No.1 is misplaced. While the said circular governs the interse
obligations between the airline and travel agents, it does not curtail the
jurisdiction of the Consumer Forum nor absolve the Appellant of its
responsibility towards the consumer. The Complainant, having availed the
services of the Appellant, cannot be compelled to pursue remedies solely
against the airlines. Hence, we do not find any illegality or irregularity in
the order of the District Commission in holding both Opposite Parties 1
and 2 jointly and severally liable for the deficiency of service in refunding
the ticket amount to the Complainant.
13. Point No.(iii):
The Appellant contended that the CEO was not responsible for the
day-to-day affairs of the organization and he was unnecessarily impleaded
and the complaint suffers from misjoinder of necessary parties.
On a perusal of the complaint, it is seen that there were no specific
allegations of personal involvement, negliegence or malafide conduct
attributed to the CEO of the Appellant Company. The CEO has been
arrayed only by designation. It is a settled law that officers of the
Company cannot be held personally liable in the absence of specific
pleadings and proof. Therefore, fastening liability on the CEO is not legally
sustainable.
14. Point No.(iv):
In view of the above findings, the finding of deficiency in service
against the travel agency warrants no interference. However, the direction
against the CEO is liable to be set aside.
9
15. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed with the following
directions:
(1) The impugned order of the District Commission is confirmed insofar
 as it relates to the Appellant travel agency.
(2) The direction fastening liability on the CEO of the Appellant
 Company is hereby set aside.
(3) The rest of the order including refund, compensation and costs
 stands affirmed.
(4) No order as to further costs in the appeal.
(5) The Complainant is permitted to withdraw the statutory deposit
 made to the credit of this appeal together with accrued interest, if
 any, towards part satisfaction after lapse of appeal/revision time.

corrected by me and pronounced by us in the open Court on this the 19th
day of May,2026.
